_comment: CitedRx social content queue. Each entry is one static post, cross-posted to Facebook and Instagram by social/post.py. Add new entries at the end; the posting script always takes the oldest entry with post_status 'ready'. Never invent facts here: every claim must trace back to a real, already-published CitedRx page (see source_url).

posts.image_headline: Is it really the same drug?
posts.image_subhead: Compounded semaglutide ≠ FDA-approved Ozempic or Wegovy
posts.caption_base:
A lot of lower-cost GLP-1 telehealth plans use compounded semaglutide — made by a compounding pharmacy, not the original manufacturer. It's not the same FDA-approved product tested in the STEP and SURMOUNT trials, and the FDA has published specific concerns about unapproved GLP-1 drugs sold for weight loss. That doesn't automatically make it unsafe — but it does mean the clinical trial evidence doesn't transfer over automatically. Know which one you're actually being prescribed before you start.

We break down which of the 21 GLP-1 telehealth providers we track are branded, mixed, or compounded-primary — link in bio.

posts.image_subhead: CitedRx's #1-ranked GLP-1 telehealth provider, out of 21
posts.caption_base:
Ro prescribes predominantly FDA-approved branded GLP-1s — Wegovy, Zepbound, and Ozempic — the exact medications tested in the STEP and SURMOUNT trials. Add a dedicated prior-authorization team for insured members and a 4.4/5 U.S. News rating, and it's our top evidence-match score in the category.

Ro isn't a CitedRx referral partner — this review wasn't paid for or reviewed by Ro. Full review in bio.

posts.image_subhead: FTC + Utah AG sued Hims & Hers in July 2026
posts.caption_base:
Before you sign up for an ED or weight-loss telehealth subscription, here's something worth knowing: in July 2026, the FTC and the Utah Attorney General sued Hims & Hers Health, alleging a deceptive multi-step cancellation process and improper sharing of health data with advertisers. Hims disputes the claims, and the case is unresolved.

We still rank Hims #1 in erectile dysfunction (8.8/10, down from 9.1 before this came to light) — but we think you should know what you're signing up for before you do. Full breakdown in bio.

posts.image_subhead: Same thing, different words — legal in all 50 states
posts.caption_base:
Estrogen and progesterone aren't controlled substances, so licensed clinicians can evaluate and prescribe menopause hormone therapy remotely almost anywhere in the U.S. — no in-person visit required.

We've scored 9 menopause/HRT telehealth providers on evidence match, independent ratings, insurance support, and more. If you've been putting off looking into HRT because you assumed it meant a string of in-person visits, it might be easier than you think. Link in bio.

posts.image_subhead: Nationwide vs. ~10 states — here's what actually matters
posts.caption_base:
Both are real trans-specialty telehealth practices using an informed-consent model for gender-affirming hormone therapy. The biggest practical difference: QueerMed serves patients nationwide; QueerDoc is licensed in roughly 10 states.

If QueerDoc serves your state, it's a legitimate option with a broader scope (puberty blockers, legal transition consults, surgery referrals). If it doesn't, QueerMed is the closest like-for-like alternative. Full factor-by-factor comparison in bio.

posts.image_subhead: Eli Lilly's lawsuit against Henry Meds is heading to trial
posts.caption_base:
Eli Lilly's lawsuit against Henry Meds — over marketing compounded tirzepatide as "personalized" medicine — is heading toward trial: a federal judge denied Henry Meds' motion to dismiss on September 24, 2026.

Henry Meds ranks 21st of the 21 GLP-1 telehealth providers we track (2.3/10), largely for this exact reason: no major GLP-1 clinical trial has tested a compounded formulation, so the evidence doesn't transfer the way it does for branded-primary providers.

Full regulatory breakdown of all 21 providers — link in bio.

posts.image_subhead: One of these had a $7.8M FTC settlement
posts.caption_base:
Talkspace (7.3/10) and BetterHelp (7.1/10) are nearly tied on CitedRx Score — but only one has a federal enforcement record. In 2023, the FTC settled with BetterHelp for $7.8M over sharing users' mental-health questionnaire answers with advertisers, including Facebook and Snapchat, without adequate consent.

The other practical difference: Talkspace accepts insurance more broadly, while BetterHelp generally doesn't bill insurance directly.

Full comparison — pricing, insurance, and the FTC settlement details — link in bio.

posts.image_subhead: The lifespan data comes from mice, not people
posts.caption_base:
NPR recently asked the question most NAD+ ads skip over: does it actually work? Here's the trail. The "~20% longer lifespan" stat behind a lot of NMN marketing comes from a single 2024 study — in mice bred for premature aging, not normal aging, and not humans.

What IS proven in people: NMN safely raises NAD+ blood levels at doses up to 1,250mg/day. That's real. Lifespan extension isn't tested in humans yet, for any brand.

We broke down every human trial, plus NMN's wild 2022→2025 legal rollercoaster with the FDA — link in bio.

posts.image_subhead: It depends entirely on which provider you pick
posts.caption_base:
Insurance coverage for gender-affirming hormone therapy isn't one-size-fits-all — it comes down to which telehealth provider you choose. FOLX Health, Transhealth, and Circle Medical bill major insurance directly. QueerMed and QueerDoc run mostly sliding-scale self-pay, though labs and prescriptions can sometimes still go through insurance.

Same category, very different costs depending on where you start.

We break down all 6 providers we track — coverage model, state availability, and CitedRx Score — link in bio.

The 2023 TRAVERSE trial followed 5,246 men and found testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) was no worse than placebo for major cardiovascular events (7.0% vs. 7.3%) — a finding that surprised a lot of doctors who'd been cautious about TRT for exactly that reason.

But there's a catch: TRT is FDA-approved specifically for hypogonadism — lab-confirmed low testosterone plus symptoms — not just "feeling low energy." A provider skipping bloodwork before prescribing is working outside what TRAVERSE, or any trial, actually studied.

We score 9 TRT telehealth providers on exactly that distinction — who requires labs, who doesn't. Link in bio.

posts.image_headline: The FDA just reversed 20 years of fear
posts.image_subhead: HRT's black-box warning is gone. Here's why.
posts.caption_base:
In February 2026, the FDA approved label changes removing boxed-warning language on cardiovascular disease, breast cancer, and dementia from several menopausal hormone therapy products — the same warning that triggered a 20-year drop in HRT use after one 2002 study.

That study (WHI) was real, but its average participant was 63 — a decade past typical menopause onset. Reanalyzed by age, the picture looks very different for women starting HRT within 10 years of menopause.

NAMS and ACOG are clear: this isn't "risk-free," just re-evaluated. We broke down all 9 menopause telehealth providers on how closely their prescribing follows the current evidence — link in bio.

posts.image_subhead: Here's why it still ranks first
posts.caption_base:
Hims ranks #1 of 10 ED telehealth providers we track (8.8/10) — but its Trustpilot rating is just 3.0/5 across roughly 8,000 reviews, the lowest of any top-tier provider we compare.

How both can be true: our CitedRx Score weighs evidence match, regulatory standing, and clinical model far more heavily than star ratings alone — and yes, that score already reflects a real deduction for the FTC and Utah Attorney General's July 2026 lawsuit over Hims's cancellation practices and data sharing.

Full methodology and the complete review — link in bio.
